comment: Stage 1 requirements: the Owner measures progress by requirements closed, not by issues or PRs (Owner, 2026-10-28; agents/program.md 0.4). Library features come from tools/catalog.py (one per algorithm); each is done when it behaves as libwebrtc M157: ported faithfully from compare/webrtc/reference/, its defaults equal libwebrtc's, and no open item labelled req:<id> remains (so no parity gap it owns is open). Status: unassessed | open | in-progress | done. The Coordinator keeps it current; tools/requirements_report.py reports it. Fields: start / end (YYYY-MM-DD; end with a leading ~ is planned), depends_on (requirement ids that must be done first), cost (the Coordinator's estimate in Fixer runs, e.g. "4 runs"). The dashboard fills a blank start from the first req:<id> item and shows merged PRs as the actual cost.
library_acceptance: Behaves as libwebrtc M157: (a) ported as a unit from compare/webrtc/reference/ (or a recorded, approved deviation), (b) defaults equal libwebrtc's, (c) no open item labelled req:<id>, so every parity gap it owns is closed or explained.

requirements.title: NACK + RTX retransmission
requirements.evidence: `NackTracker` is libwebrtc's `NackRequester` (#23; kMaxPacketAge 10000, kMaxNackPackets 1000, 100 retries without a keyframe request, `ClearUpTo`, NACK on the revealing packet #435, 20 ms tick on its grid #518) and `RtxSender` is `RtpPacketHistory` (#76 group 2: stored at pacer send, 600/9600, max(3xRTT, 1 s), `VerifyRtt`, acked culling; early resend #217; payload padding #120); defaults match. Remaining: `recovered_list_` (the receiver passes no recovered flag, `src/rtp/rtp_receiver.cc:211`) and a 20 ms `min_retry_interval` floor libwebrtc lacks. Open: #411 (D2, D5/D6 NACK/RTX cells), #437 (late retransmissions at 100 kbps), #492 (repair path around the handover outage).

requirements.title: Forward error correction (ULPFEC over RED, as libwebrtc)
requirements.evidence: ULPFEC over RED ported from M157 (#29: generator, receiver, header reader/writer, random and bursty tables, `BuildRedPayload`, RED over RTX), interop-checked both ways (`compare/webrtc/rtcp_interop.cc`); `ShouldDisableRedAndUlpfec` duplicated (#7), so no video FEC beside NACK for H.264 as libwebrtc. Remaining (parity 3.2): FEC queued after a release leaves on the next pacer pass; one RTX payload type besides RED's; FEC not in the SR packet count. #492 owns the `issue_29_ulpfec_over_red` cells.

requirements.title: RED audio redundancy (RFC 2198)
requirements.evidence: `RedEncoder`/`RedReceiver` checked equal to `audio_encoder_copy_red.cc` (parity 3.3 `same`: distance 1, 1024-byte cap, 14-bit offset, RFC 2198); the bench encodes with libopus 55513e81 with in-band FEC (#457) and the loss input ported (#62). Open: the Opus loss input (and so LBRR) moves where libwebrtc's doesn't, because our audio report block rides every video RTCP packet (#484, #504 difference 1).

requirements.title: Packet loss concealment (PCM domain)
requirements.evidence: In the call, concealment is NetEq's (`Expand`, `RandomVector`, `BackgroundNoise`, `Merge`, `Normal`, time stretch in `src/timing/neteq_expand.cc`, #62; `neteq v2` default in the session and bench). But the feature's module `loss::PacketLossConcealer` (pitch repeat, own fades) is not libwebrtc's, has no recorded deviation, is still the v1 path and the v2 fallback for leftovers under 10 ms (`src/timing/audio_jitter_buffer.cc:474-479`), and a bare `AudioJitterBufferConfig` defaults to version 1. The `issue_533` `audio.concealed_pct` gap (33.5 vs 28.9) is owned by #504, whose text names no concealment mechanism. Filed #568.

requirements.title: Keyframe requests (PLI/FIR) and loss notification
requirements.evidence: Receiver triggers ported from `RtpVideoStreamReceiver2`/`video_receive_stream2` (#23, PR #95, #335; v1 deleted in #167): first frame not a keyframe, NACK-list overflow, packet buffer cleared, IDR without parameter sets, decode time-out 200 ms / 3 s / 5 s; the sender's 300 ms `EncoderRtcpFeedback` filter (#151). Library defaults differ: `VideoSendControllerConfig::min_keyframe_request_interval` 0 (off; only the bench sets 300 ms) and `KeyframeRequestConfig::send_lntf` true (libwebrtc sends no LNTF for H.264; the bench turns it off). Not ported: sequence-discontinuity re-request, missing-video-structure trigger. Open: #480 (switches not at libwebrtc's default), #492 (keyframe path around the handover outage), #474 F3 (policer keyframe requests).

requirements.title: Temporal scalability (L1T2/L1T3)
requirements.evidence: Removed by #572 (`include/sm/loss/temporal_layers.h`: `TemporalLayerFilter` on the Builder's decision on #566, SFU-only under the one-to-one rule; `TemporalLayerScheduler` on the Owner's A on #566, single-layer H.264 in M157 has no temporal layers). Parity 3.6 rows marked `removed`; catalog 3.6 moved to the not-implemented list.

requirements.title: NACK/FEC protection selection
requirements.evidence: `FecControllerDefault`, `VCMLossProtectionLogic`, `VCMNackFecMethod` and `kFecRateTable` ported value for value (#29), driven by `rtp::Session` on target, loss and RTT; the 0.5 protection share with `send_rate_stats` (#224, on). Remaining (parity 3.7): sent frame rate counted over the last second (libwebrtc's `SendStatisticsProxy` tracker not in reference/). The FEC amount differs on `issue_29_ulpfec_over_red` (`video.avg_kbps` behind 48/80), owned by #492 (and #514).

requirements.title: Packet buffer: reordering, de-duplication, frame assembly
requirements.evidence: libwebrtc's `PacketBuffer` is ported (`src/timing/packet_buffer.cc`: 512 slots doubling to 2048, clear with a keyframe request, restart, #76 group 6; `ClearTo` and the padding window, #101; the H.264 `missing_packets_` hold, #453, on for H.264 as libwebrtc). Remaining (parity doc 4.3 'port (remaining listed)'): our H.264 assembly rule (`may_continue_frame`) not compared with `h26x_packet_buffer.cc`; packets leave at frame assembly. Open: #492 (cells opened by the H.264 receive flip), #437 (late retransmissions at the packet buffer), #411 D1 (first-frame path).

requirements.title: RTCP statistics: loss, jitter and RTT
requirements.evidence: `ReceiverStatistics` (`src/timing/rtcp_stats.cc`) has `StreamStatisticianImpl`'s guards (#76 group 5: Q4 jitter, in-order new-timestamp packets, 5 s jump skip), `ReviseFrequencyAndJitter` (#101) and the `CompactNtpRttToTimeDelta` 1 ms floor; no switch. Short: the `RttEstimator` row is 'not compared (aggregation)' (ours a 7/8-smoothed value and a minimum) and lists libwebrtc's whole-ms RTT rounding for the controller as remaining; the 'ReceiverStatistics jitter' row's status is stale ('port', text says ported). No open item serves it; filed #568.

requirements.title: Audio target delay estimation (DelayManager)
requirements.evidence: `NetEqDelayManager` (`src/timing/neteq_delay.cc`) ports M157's histogram, underrun/reorder optimizers, packet arrival history, `delay_manager` and `delay_constraints`, with libwebrtc's unit tests (#62); default in the session and the test bench (`neteq v2`). A bare `AudioJitterBufferConfig` still defaults to version 1 (`audio_jitter_buffer.h:70`). Open: #504 difference 2 (NetEq target and buffer level on `audio_only_lossy`; owns the `audio.jb_delay_p95_ms` cells); #480 (NetEq config, v1|v2 defaults).

requirements.title: Time stretching (WSOLA accelerate / preemptive expand)
requirements.evidence: libwebrtc's `time_stretch.cc`, `accelerate.cc`, `preemptive_expand.cc` are ported as `NetEqTimeStretch` (`src/timing/neteq_expand.cc`, #62), the session and test bench default (`neteq v2`); the catalog's v1 WSOLA (`src/timing/time_stretch.cc`) has no libwebrtc counterpart and is still what a bare `AudioJitterBufferConfig` (version 1) runs. Since #644 the DSP is libwebrtc's fixed point and bit-exact with its sources compiled from reference/ (`NetEqTimeStretch, BitExactWithLibwebrtc`). #480 inventories v1|v2 defaults that are not libwebrtc's.

requirements.title: Adaptive audio jitter buffer (NetEq-lite)
requirements.evidence: NetEq v2 (#62): `DecisionLogic`, `BufferLevelFilter`, `Expand`, `Merge`, `Normal`, `BackgroundNoise`, time stretch, the 200-packet buffer with full flush (#331) and Opus in-band FEC priority; default in the session and test bench (a bare config is still v1). Remaining: comfort noise/DTX not compared (`comfort_noise.cc` not ported), decode-on-insert instead of NetEq's decode loop ('port (model)'), float DSP. Open: #504 (NetEq delay cells), #480 (NetEq config and the v1 default).

requirements.title: Video jitter estimation and render timing
requirements.evidence: Timing v2 (#24, `include/sm/timing/vcm_timing.h`) ports M157's `JitterEstimator` (Kalman filter, inter-frame delay variation, `RttFilter`, 2.33 sigma - 30 ms, 10 ms OS jitter, 0.9 x RTT after 3 NACKed frames), `TimestampExtrapolator`, `DecodeTimePercentileFilter`, `VCMTiming`; default in the session and test bench. The library's own `VideoTimingConfig` still defaults to version 1 (3 sigma - 0, `video_jitter_estimator.h:78`), the v1|v2 default #480 inventories; parity rows 4.1/4.2 are stale (describe v1).

requirements.title: Clock drift estimation and compensation
requirements.evidence: Removed by #590 (`include/sm/timing/clock_drift.h`: `ClockDriftEstimator`, `RlsLineFit`, `DriftCompensator`, with their tests and benchmarks) on the Owner's A on #566: libwebrtc M157's one-to-one call has no such component and absorbs drift with NetEq's time stretch and the `rtp_to_ntp_estimator`/`timestamp_extrapolator`; nothing in `rtp::Session`, the test bench, `web/` or `compare/` used it. Parity row marked `removed`; catalog 4.7 moved to the not-implemented list.

requirements.title: Transport-wide CC feedback (and REMB)
requirements.evidence: The transport-cc wire format is interop-checked (`compare/webrtc/rtcp_interop.cc`), the receiver's generator is libwebrtc's `TransportSequenceNumberFeedbackGenerator` (500 ms back window, 5% interval, 100 ms first report; #76, #217), and the sender joins history and feedback as `TransportFeedbackAdapter` (#602, #569 part 2: 60 s history window, in-flight above the last acked sequence number, local receive-time base with `GetBaseDelta`'s 24-bit wrap checked against `rtcp_packet/transport_feedback.cc`, #608; feedback that finds no packet is not passed on). REMB feeds `SendSideBandwidthEstimation`'s upper limit (#61). Not ported, no effect on a one-to-one call: the per-`NetworkRoute` map (one route), RFC 8888 feedback (off by default in M157), `pending_untracked_size_` (the session numbers every packet), `ambiguous_receive_time` (unused by GoogCC M157).

requirements.title: Delay-based bandwidth estimation (GCC)
requirements.evidence: Ported as a unit from `goog_cc` (`InterArrivalDelta`, trendline, #19; `AimdRateControl`, `LinkCapacityEstimator`, #15; `AlrDetector`, #48/#152; `RobustThroughputEstimator`, #150), with libwebrtc's unit tests (#166); v1 deleted (#167). The library default `GccConfig::max_rate` is now unbounded as libwebrtc's (#639, #580). The Fixer's seed-1 trace on #611 found the detector's rows (trend, threshold, send/recv deltas) identical to libwebrtc's to 4 decimals until an upstream 1-byte input difference.

requirements.title: Loss-based bandwidth estimation
requirements.evidence: `LossBasedBweV2` with `CreateConfig` defaults and `SendSideBandwidthEstimation` with `RttBasedBackoff` on as M157 (#12); v1 loss bands deleted (#167); no switch. Open: #536 (target collapses to 110-430 kbps at 20% loss, not yet measured on libwebrtc), #461 (unit rounding in `loss_based_bwe_v2.cc`).

requirements.title: Send-side bandwidth estimation (GCC network controller)
requirements.evidence: `GoogCcNetworkController` glue ported (#61: pacing rates, pacing factor #187, cwnd pushback #446, `CongestionControlHandler` on by default, `ConvertConstraints` #464), unit tests ported (#166). Remaining: `SendSideController` composition 'not compared' (parity doc 9.3), fixed 24 B RTP overhead, `GccConfig::max_rate` 10 Mbps. Open: #522 (rate held through an outage onto a slower link), #536, #411 D4, #480.

requirements.title: Pacer with priority queues
requirements.evidence: `PacingController`, `PrioritizedPacketQueue`, `BitrateProber`, `TaskQueuePacedSender` scheduling (#70, #48, #123) and padding through `RtpSender::GeneratePadding` (#120) ported with libwebrtc's unit tests (#166). The keyframe flush of queued RTX padding (`pacing_controller.cc:227-231`) is behind `keyframe_flush_padding`, off by default (#437, #480). Open also: #514 (media-SSRC and audio-only padding), #536 (queue grows to 2 s at 20% loss), #461 (`DataRate * TimeDelta` rounding).

requirements.title: Bandwidth probing
requirements.evidence: `ProbeController`, `ProbeBitrateEstimator` and `BitrateProber` (#48), `AlrDetector` with libwebrtc's defaults (#152), call-start ALR probing for audio only (#62, #355); v1 deleted (#167); defaults as libwebrtc. Open: #514 (probe/ALR padding count and sizes on NACK-off and audio-only calls), #461 (rounding in `probing.cc`).

requirements.title: Bitrate allocation among streams
requirements.evidence: `BitrateAllocator` ported (`include/sm/cc/bitrate_allocator_v2.h`, #104: low/normal/max allocation, hysteresis, `min_total_allocated_bitrate`, max padding; encoder activity time-out #375); v1 deleted (#167). Short: libwebrtc's `AudioSendStream::GetMinMaxBitrateConstraints` (`audio_send_stream.cc:808-901`, in reference/) adds per-packet overhead over the Opus frame-length range, where `rtp::Session::AddAudioSend` hands a fixed `allocation_rate` (audio 49.6 vs libwebrtc 39.2 kbps, #196/#151). No open item; filed #569.

requirements.title: Encoder overshoot control (frame dropper)
requirements.evidence: `FrameDropper` (#5, `same`), `EncoderOvershootDetector`/`EncoderBitrateAdjuster` (#5) with link headroom (#326), reconfigure reset (#346), `RateUtilizationTracker` (#355), all on by default. Short (parity row still `port`): rates are adjusted per captured frame, not on each bitrate update as `VideoStreamEncoder::OnBitrateUpdated`/`SetEncoderRates`; one stream / one temporal layer only, not recorded. The `issue_466_*` overshoot gaps carry #466's note. No open item; filed #569.

requirements.title: Resolution/frame-rate adaptation and CPU overuse detection
requirements.evidence: The send path runs libwebrtc's adaptation behind `quality_scaling` (on by default): `QualityScaler` v2, `EncodeUsageResource`, `OveruseFrameDetector` (`SendProcessingUsage1`), `ResourceAdaptationProcessor`, initial frame drop, MAINTAIN_FRAMERATE (#84). Library defaults not libwebrtc's: `cc::CpuOveruseConfig` version 1, the `DegradationController` bpp ladder, camera default balanced. Not ported: `BitrateConstraint`, the initial-drop start-bitrate reset, `pending_frame_`. #480 names adaptation in its inventory.

requirements.title: Link outage detection and recovery
requirements.evidence: As libwebrtc, the sender takes no action on an outage (#151, PR #184, Owner sign-off): the encoder runs, the cwnd drops frames, the receiver's decode time-out asks for the keyframe; `cc::OutageMonitor` only observes (its parity row still asks for an Owner decision, #20). Open: #522 (an outage onto a slower link: no rate cut while feedback is missing, then the drain), #411 (D8 and the `cc.max_settle_ms` cells after outages).

requirements.title: Acoustic echo cancellation
requirements.evidence: AEC3 is ported whole from `reference/modules/audio_processing/aec3` (#240 steps 1-6, incl. `OouraFft`; `include/sm/audio/aec3*.h`), libwebrtc's unit tests pass and `E2E_EchoCanceller.Aec3FullDuplexCallAsLibwebrtc` reaches M157's ERLE. But it runs only with `apm v2`, which defaults to off (`ChainConfig::apm_v2 = false`, `tests/e2e/audio_sims.h:98`); the v1 PBFDAF `audio::EchoCanceller` is still the catalog unit and the benches' path. Not ported: `MultiChannelContentDetector`/`ConfigSelector`, `AlignmentMixer`. Neither bench call runs APM. No open item; filed #565.

requirements.title: Echo-path delay estimation
requirements.evidence: AEC3's delay estimation (decimator, matched filter, lag aggregator, clock-drift detector, render delay controller) is ported (`include/sm/audio/aec3_delay.h`, #240 step 1) and used inside `EchoCanceller3`, but only under `apm v2` (default off); the v1 GCC-PHAT `EchoDelayEstimator` is the catalog unit. Mono only. Parity row and catalog note are stale. No open item; filed #565.

requirements.title: Noise suppression
requirements.evidence: libwebrtc's NS is ported whole (`ns::NoiseSuppressor`, `include/sm/audio/ns.h`, #241), bit-exact with M157 at 16/32/48 kHz, default level k18dB as libwebrtc. It runs only under `apm v2` (default off); the v1 STFT-Wiener `audio::NoiseSuppressor` is the default. The parity row's 'default flip with #240, #242' never happened. No open item; filed #565.

requirements.title: Automatic gain control and limiter
requirements.evidence: AGC1 (`agc1.h` digital stage bit-exact, `agc1_vad.h`, `AgcManagerDirect`/`MonoAgc`, `CaptureLevelsAdjuster`, clipping predictor off as libwebrtc) and AGC2 with its RNN VAD are ported (#242); the apm v2 chain matches libwebrtc AGC1. Default is still the v1 `AutomaticGainControl`/`Limiter` (`apm v2` off). AGC2's RNN VAD is float-close, not bit-exact (PFFFT). No open item; filed #565.

requirements.title: High-pass filter
requirements.evidence: libwebrtc's `HighPassFilter`/`CascadedBiquadFilter` are ported with their coefficients (`include/sm/audio/hpf.h`, #239; 67.2 dB hum attenuation as libwebrtc), but the default is the v1 4th-order Butterworth (16.4 dB) because `apm v2` is off. No open item; filed #565.

requirements.title: Transient (keyboard click) suppression
requirements.evidence: M157's APM has no transient suppressor (deprecated `TransientSuppression.enabled` false); ours is off by default (`TransientSuppressorConfig::enabled = false`) and passes audio unchanged (`TransientSuppressor.OffByDefaultAsLibwebrtc`, #243). Keeping it as an opt-in is the Owner's decision of 2026-10-22 (catalog notes; parity doc 6.2 'opt-in is a deviation the Owner approved'). No open item.

requirements.title: DTX and comfort noise (RFC 3389)
requirements.evidence: Removed by #591 (`include/sm/audio/comfort_noise.h`: `DtxController` and the RFC 3389 comfort-noise generator, on the Owner's A on #566: libwebrtc M157's one-to-one call has no such component on the Opus path, whose DTX is off without `usedtx=1`, as the bench's `kDtx=false`). Parity doc 6.3 item 1 marked removed; catalog 6.7 moved to the not-implemented list.

requirements.title: Voice activity detection
requirements.evidence: The catalog unit is the v1 energy/spectral-flatness `Vad` (`include/sm/audio/vad.h`), not libwebrtc's; libwebrtc's `WebRtcVad` and `VoiceActivityDetector` are ported only inside AGC1's loudness meter (`agc1_vad.h`, #242). The v1 `Vad` still drives the e2e chain and the transient suppressor. Parity row stale (files now in reference/). Filed #565.

requirements.title: Audio level (RFC 6464)
requirements.evidence: `AudioLevelMeter` ports `voe::AudioLevel` (#101) for stats, but the RFC 6464 byte comes from our per-frame float RMS (`src/audio/audio_level.cc:17`), where `ChannelSend` writes `RmsLevel::Average()` over the packet's 10 ms frames with muted handling (`reference/audio/channel_send.cc:391-393, 915-921`; `rms_level.cc` not in reference/). Neither harness registers the extension. Filed #567.

requirements.title: Sample-rate conversion
requirements.evidence: The catalog unit is the v1 polyphase Kaiser `Resampler`, not libwebrtc's. `SincResampler`/`PushSincResampler` are ported (`include/sm/audio/sinc_resampler.h`, #242) and used by the bench's Opus decoder, but `common_audio/resampler/resampler.cc` and `push_resampler.cc` (now in reference/) are not ported. Parity row stale. Filed #565.

requirements.title: Band splitting
requirements.evidence: `SplittingFilter` and `ThreeBandFilterBank` ported from `splitting_filter.cc`, `three_band_filter_bank.cc` and `common_audio/signal_processing/splitting_filter.c` with their coefficients (#241), bit-exact with libwebrtc's code built from reference/ (`SplittingFilter.MatchesLibwebrtcOutput`); no switch. Mono instances (one per channel gives the same result). No open item.

requirements.title: Freeze detection
requirements.evidence: #268 ported libwebrtc's freeze rule from `video/video_quality_observer2.cc` (whole-ms intervals, 30-interval average from the 5th, `max(3 x avg, avg + 150 ms)`, 5 s pause; constants in `include/sm/video/freeze_detector.h`, no switch); parity-doc 7.1 row `same`, `sm_video_compare` matches on every input. The harness feeds libwebrtc's rendered frames to this same detector. The freeze-metric gaps come from upstream mechanisms owned by #437, #411, #474; no open item names the detector.

requirements.title: Hardware -> software codec fallback
requirements.evidence: Ported from libwebrtc M157: #605 (#573) `VideoEncoderSoftwareFallbackWrapper` (`api/video_codecs/video_encoder_software_fallback_wrapper.cc`: fallback on init failure or `FALLBACK_SOFTWARE`, sticky until `Release`, rates/RTT/loss primed on switch, forced-fallback field trials off by default) and #627 (#607) `VideoDecoderSoftwareFallbackWrapper` (`video_decoder_software_fallback_wrapper.cc`: `FALLBACK_SOFTWARE` or the 4th consecutive keyframe error, sticky until `Release`, forced trial off). The app runs the codecs (program.md 0.1). Not ported: the temporal-layer forced switch (temporal layers removed, #572) and the `OnLossNotification` replay (no encoder loss-notification input). Not on the bench call path, so no parity cell.

requirements.title: Video orientation (CVO)
requirements.evidence: `video/orientation.{h,cc}` codes the TS 26.114 CVO byte (parity doc 7.3 `same (wire format)`, from the spec; `rtp_header_extensions.cc`/`rtp_cvo.h` not in reference/). Our RTP sender never writes CVO, where `rtp_sender_video.cc:401-408` sets it on a keyframe's last packet or when the rotation changes or is non-zero. No open item; filed #567.

requirements.title: Content hints and screen-content variable frame rate
requirements.evidence: `SettingsFor` (`src/video/content_policy.cc`) maps camera video with no hint to balanced, where libwebrtc's `GetDegradationPreference` (`webrtc_video_engine.cc`) defaults to MAINTAIN_FRAMERATE; its QP ceilings and fps floors have no libwebrtc counterpart (parity doc 7.2 'deviation to decide'); `FrameChangeDetector` waits on a screen-share scope decision. The send path itself hard-codes MAINTAIN_FRAMERATE. #480's inventory names the degradation preference.

requirements.title: Codec negotiation
requirements.evidence: Removed by #592 (`include/sm/video/codec_negotiation.h`: `NegotiateCodecs`, `ParseH264ProfileLevelId`) on the Owner's A on #566: SDP offer/answer stays with the host stack (program.md 0.1); libwebrtc's codec lists live in `webrtc_video_engine.cc`, outside the call path. Parity 7.3 row marked `removed`; catalog 7.5 moved to the not-implemented list.

requirements.title: Resolution scaling and aspect handling
requirements.evidence: Removed by #593 (`include/sm/video/frame_scaler.h`: `Scale`, `ScaleToFit`, `Crop`, on the Owner's A on #566: libwebrtc M157's one-to-one call has no such component; it scales with libyuv's `I420Buffer::Scale` and the frames are the app's). Parity doc 7.3 row marked removed; catalog 7.6 moved to the not-implemented list.

requirements.title: Render timing and late-frame dropping
requirements.evidence: Timing v2 (#24: `FrameReleaseController`, VCMTiming, frame-decode timing, time-out tracker) is the default in `SessionConfig::timing` and the test bench. The pre-render queue `video::RenderFrames` (port of `incoming_video_stream.cc`/`video_render_frames.cc`, #459) is **off** by default (`render_smoothing`, `include/sm/rtp/session.h:138`) where libwebrtc's `enable_prerenderer_smoothing` is on (`video_receive_stream2.cc:400`); `keyframe_flush_padding` is off too. Both are #437's, and #480 lists `render_smoothing` first. The `very_low_capacity` freeze and render-fps gaps are owned by #437/#411.

requirements.title: QP-based quality scaler
requirements.evidence: `QualityScaler` v2 is M157's `quality_scaler.cc` with QualityScalingExperiment's smoothers (#84), wired with `VideoStreamAdapter`, `VideoAdapter`, the CPU resource and `ResourceAdaptationProcessor` into `VideoSendController`; `quality_scaling` on by default, as libwebrtc's MAINTAIN_FRAMERATE. Remaining: standalone `QualityScalerConfig::version` defaults to 1 (the send path sets 2); BALANCED/MAINTAIN_RESOLUTION steps, resource removal, the start-bitrate initial-drop reset and `pending_frame_` not ported. #480's inventory names adaptation (quality scaler, CPU overuse, degradation preference).

requirements.title: RTP -> NTP mapping
requirements.evidence: #77 ported `RtpToNtpEstimator` from M157 `rtc_base/rtp_to_ntp_estimator.cc` as a unit (`src/sync/rtp_to_ntp.cc`); every row of docs/design/libwebrtc-parity.md 8.1 is `same` (regression over 20 SRs, duplicate check, invalid-SR rejection, Unwrap). No switch: it runs whenever lip sync runs (`av_sync` on by default in the test bench, as libwebrtc with a sync group). No open stage-1 item serves it.

requirements.title: Audio/video synchronization and CNAME sync groups
requirements.evidence: #77 (PRs #278, #300, #306) ported `StreamSynchronization`, `RtpStreamsSynchronizer` and `Syncable` (`src/sync/stream_sync.cc`); parity-doc 8.2/8.2a rows are `same` except two n/a rows and the pairing rule (`call/call.cc` not in reference/). Remaining: `stream_sync.cc` uses our truncating `ms()` where libwebrtc's `DivideRoundToNearest` rounds (#461). Defaults: `av_sync` on in the test bench; the library's `SessionConfig::av_sync` / `audio_rtcp` default false (the app opts in with a sync group, as in libwebrtc). The `sync.av_offset_p95_ms` gaps are owned by #474 (F1, congestive video lag).

requirements.title: Absolute capture time and glass-to-glass latency
requirements.evidence: Parity doc 8.3: `AbsoluteCaptureTimeSender`/`AbsoluteCaptureTimeInterpolator` are 'file needed (#57), unplaced' (ours decides per packet, libwebrtc per frame; no `CaptureClockOffsetUpdater`); the `LatencyEstimator` row is `port`, unplaced (min offset with a 5% leak vs `RemoteNtpTimeEstimator`'s median of 7 after 3 samples); `capture_to_render_ms` is a library extra libwebrtc reports only under a non-default trial (no recorded deviation). The harness never sends abs-capture-time. No open item serves it; filed #567.

requirements.title: Header extensions (RFC 8285) and BUNDLE demuxing
